title: A Biased-SECE Interface for Piezoelectric Energy Harvesting with Geometric-Mean-Computational MPPT Achieving 99.9% MPPT Efficiency, 8.75Cycles/ΔVOC Tracking, and 9.3x Energy Extraction
problem: Piezoelectric energy harvesting (PEH) systems must achieve accurate and responsive maximum-power-point (MPP) tracking; fractional open-circuit voltage (FOCV) causes energy interruption, while perturb-and-observe (P&O) and duty-cycle methods trade off tracking speed vs accuracy.
motivation: Autonomous IoT/sensor systems require sustainable energy harvesting with rapid adaptation to time-varying piezoelectric voltage and vibration patterns to maximize extracted power without sacrificing responsiveness.
method: The system combines a specialized circuit (biased-SECE, which combines switch-harvesting-on-inductor-peak or SHIP with parallel SECE) with an algorithm using geometric mean calculations to track the optimal electrical load. Rather than stopping energy extraction to measure and adjust—like traditional methods—this approach continuously adapts based on recent voltage readings. It responds to voltage changes in 8.75 cycles and achieves 99.9% efficiency, meaning it wastes almost none of the harvested energy on the tracking process itself.
key_novelty: A geometric-mean-based tracking algorithm continuously finds the optimal electrical load without pausing energy extraction, responding in just 8.75 cycles per voltage change.
limitations: Abstract-only; vibration types tested, frequency range, output power, conversion efficiency to load, and real-world deployment results not discussed.
primary_theme: Geometric-mean MPPT for continuous fast-tracking piezoelectric energy harvesting
